description: The Integrated Urban Complexity Model simulates urban growth and transformation with the objective of reducing energy used for transport. Its developers combine spatial population changes with an optimization routine and constraints such as maximum density and flood exposure. The GMD application uses Frankfurt and a one-kilometre grid; other applications require their own geographic inputs and appropriate empirical relationships. Time follows model transformation steps, not a historical observation series. The public Python repository documents installation through pip or conda and dependencies including NumPy, SciPy, xarray and visualization libraries. Source code is free under GPL-3.0, with a Zenodo release linked by the paper. IUCm supports scenario studies connecting settlement patterns, transport demand and climate adaptation. A limitation is that optimized population configurations depend on simplified empirical relationships and constraints; they are not predictions of household choices or implementation feasibility. No directly related existing catalogue record was established. This review read the article availability and repository documentation without running the model.
